questions.q: When did Abijah begin to reign over Judah?
questions.a: Abijah began to reign over Judah in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam.

questions.q: How long did Abijah rule in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Abijah ruled in Jerusalem for three years.

questions.q: Was Abijah’s heart devoted to Yahweh his God?
questions.a: Abijah’s heart was not devoted to Yahweh his God.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh raise up a son for Abijah in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh raised up a son for Abijah for the sake of David.

questions.q: In what matter did David turn away from Yahweh?
questions.a: David only turned away from Yahweh in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

questions.q: What happened all the days of Abijah’s life?
questions.a: There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of Abijah’s life.

questions.q: When Abijah slept with his fathers, who became king in his place?
questions.a: When Abijah slept with his fathers, Asa became king in his place.

questions.q: When did Asa begin to reign over Judah?
questions.a: Asa began to reign over Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel.

questions.q: How many years did Asa reign in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Asa reigned 41 years in Jerusalem.

questions.q: What did Asa do in the eyes of Yahweh?
questions.a: Asa did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh, as David had done.

questions.q: What did Asa do in the land?
questions.a: Asa removed the male prostitutes and the idols his ancestors had made in the land.

questions.q: Whom did Asa remove from being queen?
questions.a: Asa removed his own grandmother Maacah from being queen.

questions.q: What was the condition of Asa’s heart toward Yahweh?
questions.a: Asa’s heart was completely dedicated to Yahweh all his days.

questions.q: What did Asa bring into the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: Asa brought all the items that his father had dedicated to God and all the gold and silver things that he had dedicated to God into the house of Yahweh.

questions.q: With whom was Asa at war?
questions.a: Asa was at war with Baasha king of Israel all their days.

questions.q: Why did Baasha build up Ramah?
questions.a: Baasha built up Ramah so that no one would enter into or leave the area that King Asa ruled.

questions.q: What did Asa do with all the silver and gold from the storerooms of the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: Asa sent the silver and gold to Ben Hadad, the grandson of the king of Aram, who lived in Damascus.

questions.q: What did Asa say to Benhadad?
questions.a: Asa said to Benhadad, “Let there be a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and your father.”

questions.q: What did Benhadad do after he listened to Asa?
questions.a: After he listened to Asa, Benhadad sent his armies to attack the cities of Israel.

questions.q: What did Baasha do when he heard about this?
questions.a: When Baasha heard about the attacks, he stopped building up Ramah.

questions.q: What did Asa do with the materials that had been used to build up Ramah?
questions.a: Asa took the materials that had been used to build up Ramah and used them to build up Geba and Mizpah.

questions.q: Where were all of Asa’s matters written?
questions.a: All of Asa’s matters were written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah.

questions.q: After Asa slept with his fathers, who became king in his place?
questions.a: After Asa slept with his fathers, his son Jehoshaphat became king in his place.

questions.q: Who began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa?
questions.a: Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa.

questions.q: How did Nadab walk in the sight of Yahweh?
questions.a: Nadab did evil in the sight of Yahweh and walked in the ways of his father and in his sin.

questions.q: What did Baasha son of Ahijah do at Gibbethon?
questions.a: Baasha the son of Ahijah killed Nadab at Gibbethon.

questions.q: What did Baasha do as soon as he became king?
questions.a: As soon as Baasha became king, he killed all of the family of Jeroboam. He did not leave one of Jeroboam’s descendants breathing.

questions.q: How long was there war between Asa and Baasha?
questions.a: There was war between Asa and Baasha all their days.

questions.q: How long did Baasha reign in Tirza?
questions.a: Baasha reigned in Tirza for 24 years.

questions.q: How did Baasha live?
questions.a: Baasha did evil in the sight of Yahweh and lived in the way of Jeroboam. encouraging his people to sin in the same way that he sinned.

commentary.text: Wicked reign of Abijam, king of Judah.
Good reign of Asa, king of Judah.
The evil reigns of Nadab and Baasha in Israel.

Verses 1–8 Abijam's heart was not perfect with the Lord his God; he wanted sincerity; he began well, but he fell off, and walked in all the sins of his father, following his bad example, though he had seen the bad consequences of it. David's family was continued as a lamp in Jerusalem, to maintain the true worship of God there, when the light of Divine truth was extinguished in all other places. The Lord has still taken care of his cause, while those who ought to have been serviceable thereto have lived and perished in their sins. The Son of David will still continue a light to his church, to establish it in truth and righteousness to the end of time. There are two kinds of fulfilling the law, one legal, the other by the gospel. Legal is, when men do all things required in the law, and that by themselves. None ever thus fulfilled the law but Christ, and Adam before his fall. The gospel manner of fulfilling the law is, to believe in Christ who fulfilled the law for us, and to endeavour in the whole man to obey God in all his precepts. And this is accepted of God, as to all those that are in Christ. Thus David and others are said to fulfil the law.

Asa did what was right in the eyes of the Lord. That is right indeed which is so in God's eyes. Asa's times were times of reformation. He removed that which was evil; there reformation begins, and a great deal he found to do. When Asa found idolatry in the court, he rooted it out thence. Reformation must begin at home. Asa honours and respects his mother; he loves her well, but he loves God better. Those that have power are happy when thus they have hearts to use it well. We must not only cease to do evil, but learn to do well; not only cast away the idols of our iniquity, but dedicate ourselves and our all to God's honour and glory. Asa was cordially devoted to the service of God, his sins not arising from presumption. But his league with Benhadad arose from unbelief. Even true believers find it hard, in times of urgent danger, to trust in the Lord with all their heart. Unbelief makes way for carnal policy, and thus for one sin after another. Unbelief has often led Christians to call in the help of the Lord's enemies in their contests with their brethren; and some who once shone brightly, have thus been covered with a dark cloud towards the end of their days.

During the single reign of Asa in Judah, the government of Israel was in six or seven different hands. Observe the ruin of the family of Jeroboam; no word of God shall fall to the ground. Divine threatenings are not designed merely to terrify. Ungodly men execute the just judgments of God upon each other. But in the midst of dreadful sins and this apparent confusion, the Lord carries on his own plan: when it is fully completed, the glorious justice, wisdom, truth, and mercy therein displayed, shall be admired and adored through all the ages of eternity.
